_note: Fictional internal policy written for this prototype. It is modelled on UK rules (FCA DISP, Consumer Duty, the Payment Services Regulations 2017 and the PSR APP scam reimbursement rules) but it is not legal advice and is simplified.
title: Harbour & Vale Bank Complaint Handling Policy

paragraphs.heading: What counts as a complaint
paragraphs.text: A complaint is any expression of dissatisfaction, oral or written, justified or not, about our products or service, where the customer says they have suffered, or may suffer, financial loss, material distress or material inconvenience. Staff must not ask the customer to use the word complaint before treating it as one.

paragraphs.heading: Who can complain
paragraphs.text: A complaint may be made by the customer, by someone with legal authority to act for them (an attorney, deputy or executor), or by a representative the customer has authorised in writing, including a claims management company.

paragraphs.heading: Logging
paragraphs.text: Every complaint must be logged in the CRM on the day it is received, whatever the channel, with the date received, channel, product and cause category.

paragraphs.heading: Acknowledgement
paragraphs.text: If a complaint is not resolved by the close of the third business day after it was received, we must send a prompt written acknowledgement that names the handler or team dealing with it.

paragraphs.heading: Summary resolution
paragraphs.text: A complaint resolved to the customer's satisfaction by the close of the third business day after receipt may be closed with a summary resolution communication. The communication must tell the customer they can refer the complaint to the Financial Ombudsman Service if they later become dissatisfied.

paragraphs.heading: Multiple issues
paragraphs.text: Where a customer raises more than one issue, each issue must be recorded separately with its own product and cause category, and each must be answered in the final response.

paragraphs.heading: Repeat and linked complaints
paragraphs.text: Before investigating, the handler must check for earlier complaints from the same customer on the same subject in the last twelve months and record any link.

paragraphs.heading: Standard time limit
paragraphs.text: We must send a final response within eight weeks of receiving the complaint, or a written explanation of why we cannot yet do so, with the customer's right to refer to the Financial Ombudsman Service.

paragraphs.heading: Payment services time limit
paragraphs.text: Where the complaint concerns rights and obligations under Parts 6 and 7 of the Payment Services Regulations 2017, such as an unauthorised or wrongly executed payment, the final response is due within fifteen business days. In exceptional circumstances outside our control we may extend to thirty-five business days, but only if we send a holding reply within the fifteen days explaining why.

paragraphs.heading: Mixed complaints
paragraphs.text: Where a complaint covers both payment services issues and other issues, the handler must confirm with a team leader whether the whole complaint will be answered within the payment services time limit. If unsure, the shorter time limit applies.

paragraphs.heading: Ombudsman referral
paragraphs.text: Every final response must tell the customer they have six months from the date of the final response to refer the complaint to the Financial Ombudsman Service.

paragraphs.heading: Complaints already with the Ombudsman
paragraphs.text: If the customer says the complaint is already with the Financial Ombudsman Service, the handler must record the Ombudsman reference and pass the case to the Ombudsman liaison team rather than starting a new investigation.

paragraphs.heading: Fair investigation
paragraphs.text: Every complaint must be investigated competently, diligently and impartially, using all relevant evidence, including the customer's own account, call recordings, system records and relevant policies.

paragraphs.heading: Conflicting records
paragraphs.text: Where system records disagree, for example on the date of a call or a payment, the handler must record both versions and the source of each, and must not choose between them without evidence.

paragraphs.heading: What the customer wants
paragraphs.text: The handler must record, in the customer's own words where possible, the outcome the customer is seeking.

paragraphs.heading: Decisions stay with people
paragraphs.text: Decisions on whether a complaint is upheld, and on any redress or compensation, are made only by an authorised member of staff. Automated tools may help gather and organise information but must not decide outcomes.

paragraphs.heading: Contacting the customer
paragraphs.text: Where information needed to investigate is missing, the handler must make at least one documented attempt to contact the customer before a case is passed to a specialist team.

paragraphs.heading: Recognising vulnerability
paragraphs.text: Staff must look for signs that a customer may be in vulnerable circumstances, such as bereavement, serious illness, mental health conditions, financial difficulty, domestic or economic abuse, low confidence with digital channels, or limited English.

paragraphs.heading: Recording vulnerability
paragraphs.text: Signs of vulnerability must be recorded with the customer's consent where possible, along with any support the customer needs, such as a preferred contact channel or a nominated contact.

paragraphs.heading: Adapting the handling
paragraphs.text: Vulnerability changes how a complaint is handled, not whether it is handled quickly. Where a case can be put right straight away, it should be. The handler must adapt communication and must not pass a vulnerable customer between teams without a warm handover.

paragraphs.heading: When to hand over
paragraphs.text: A complaint must be passed to a specialist team when it falls within that team's remit, using the team's handover checklist.

paragraphs.heading: Complete handovers
paragraphs.text: A handover is complete only when every required checklist item is filled in or marked as not available with a reason. The receiving team may return an incomplete handover with a coded reason.

paragraphs.heading: Telling the customer
paragraphs.text: The handler must tell the customer which team now has their complaint and record what they were told.

paragraphs.heading: Unauthorised transactions
paragraphs.text: Where a customer says they did not authorise a payment, we must refund it by the end of the next business day unless we have reasonable grounds to suspect fraud by the customer, which must be reported, or we can show the customer acted with gross negligence or intent.

paragraphs.heading: Authorised push payment scams
paragraphs.text: Where a customer was tricked into sending a Faster Payment to a fraudster, we follow the APP scam reimbursement rules. Claims made within thirteen months of the last scam payment are reimbursed up to the scheme limit of eighty-five thousand pounds unless an exception applies. We may apply an excess of up to one hundred pounds, but never to a customer in vulnerable circumstances.

paragraphs.heading: Reimbursement timing
paragraphs.text: APP scam claims must be decided within five business days. The clock may be stopped to gather information needed to assess the claim, but the total must not exceed thirty-five business days.

paragraphs.heading: Evidence for scam claims
paragraphs.text: The Fraud and Scams team needs the payment details, when the scam was reported, any warnings shown at the time, the customer's account of events in their own words, and the receiving bank.

paragraphs.heading: Bereavement
paragraphs.text: Complaints involving a deceased customer's accounts must be handled with care. Staff must confirm who has authority to act, such as the executor or administrator, before sharing account information.

paragraphs.heading: Powers of attorney
paragraphs.text: Where an attorney or deputy acts for a customer, the authority must be registered and checked before the complaint is discussed in detail. Pending registration must be recorded and does not delay the acknowledgement.

paragraphs.heading: Claims management companies
paragraphs.text: Where a claims management company complains for a customer, the handler must check the written authority covers this complaint and should still contact the customer directly where it is appropriate to do so.

paragraphs.heading: Arrears and collections
paragraphs.text: Where a complaint involves arrears or collections, the handler must check whether forbearance was considered, whether collections activity should be paused while the complaint is investigated, and whether the customer was signposted to free debt advice.

paragraphs.heading: Fees and interest during difficulty
paragraphs.text: Fees and interest applied while a customer was in financial difficulty must be reviewed as part of the complaint.

paragraphs.heading: Record keeping
paragraphs.text: Complaint records, including all evidence and the final response, must be kept for at least three years from the date the complaint was received.

paragraphs.heading: Root cause
paragraphs.text: Each complaint must be tagged with a root-cause category so that recurring problems can be found and fixed.

paragraphs.heading: Quality checks
paragraphs.text: A sample of closed complaints is checked each month by the quality team, including a check that every issue raised was answered.
